sections.h2: Taxes on a Maryland seller's closing statement
sections.html:
Expect three government charges on a Maryland settlement sheet. One is the statewide transfer tax at 0.5% of the sale consideration. The other two, a county transfer tax and a recordation tax, depend on the county.

They attach to the deed, so an agent's involvement changes nothing. The circuit court clerk also adds a recording fee and a surcharge, and the tax account must be current before the deed can go through.

  • State transfer tax: 0.5% of consideration, collected at the clerk's counter.
  • County transfer tax: each county picks a rate between 0% and 1.5%.
  • Recordation tax: a county rate applied to every $500 of consideration.
  • Recording fee and surcharge: assessed on each instrument filed.
  • Back taxes and county charges: settled first.

sections.h2: Who pays transfer and recordation taxes?
sections.html:
The default under Real Property Article 14-104 is a 50-50 split of the recordation tax and both transfer taxes. A contract or another statute can change that, and most Maryland contracts speak to it, so find that clause before signing.

A major exception applies to first-time Maryland buyers who intend to occupy the home as their principal residence. In that case the seller covers the entire State transfer tax, and the recordation and local transfer taxes as well, unless both sides agree in writing to a different arrangement.

There are conditions. Every buyer named on the deed signs a sworn statement, and with several buyers all of them must qualify. The State rate for these buyers drops to 0.25% from 0.5%, which lowers the seller's cost on that one line.

A local government may also exempt part of the recordation tax for owner-occupied homes where the buyer lives for at least 7 months of a 12 month period. Your title company or clerk will know whether your county has done so.

Rates swing widely from county to county, and an identical price can mean very different bills. Here are fiscal 2026 rates for five counties.

CountyRecordation tax (per $500)County transfer tax
Baltimore County$2.501.5%
Howard$2.501.25%
Harford$3.301.0%
Carroll$6.500.0%
Frederick$7.000.0%

Montgomery County's rate varies with property value and adds a recordation surcharge on transactions over $500,000. Anne Arundel's transfer tax runs from 1.0% to 1.5%. Across the state, recordation tax ranges from $2.50 to $7.00 per $500, and transfer tax from 0% to 1.5%.

Under the default split each side carries half. With a qualifying first-time buyer the State rate falls to 0.25% and the seller carries the whole set unless the contract says otherwise. A title company can put an estimate for your own address in writing.

Recording a typical deed of nine pages or less costs $20 at the circuit court clerk's office, and nearly every recorded instrument also carries a $40 surcharge. Harford and Howard Counties show identical figures.

  • Release of nine pages or less: $10.
  • Instrument of ten pages or more that is not a principal residence: $75.
  • Copies: $0.50 a page in Harford County, plus $5 for a certified copy.
  • Harford Land Records accepts e-records through Simplifile.

Recording fees are not refundable, and getting State transfer tax back takes a claim form filed with the clerk. If an exemption applies, the document must quote the complete exemption code, or the clerk collects full tax.

sections.h2: Property tax before the deed transfers
sections.html:
Under Real Property Article 3-104, all taxes, assessments and charges owed on the property must be paid first. The collector then endorses a certificate on the deed, and only after that is the transfer posted to the assessment books. Some counties charge up to $55 for the certificate of paid charges.

Procedures are local. Harford County sells a Certificate of Tax Liens and Other Charges Due for $50, valid 90 days, and county staff stamp each deed before recording. In Howard County, deeds pass through the Department of Finance's Division of Recordation Tax before they reach Land Records.

Back taxes catch sellers off guard more than anything else. Liens are auctioned at annual tax sales. Even then, the owner can redeem by paying the lien amount, interest and fees up to the moment a circuit judge signs a foreclosure order.

Closing paperwork goes through a tax office that collects and stamps, then the Circuit Court land records office that records. Harford and Howard show how much hours and timing can differ.

  • Harford Revenue Collections: 220 S. Main Street, Bel Air, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, with processing that usually takes 24 to 48 hours.
  • Harford Land Records: 20 West Courtland Street, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a 4:00 p.m. courier and title company cutoff.
  • Howard Division of Recordation Tax: 3430 Courthouse Drive, Ellicott City, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Howard Land Records: 9250 Judicial Way, Suite 1900, with recording hours of 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

Harford allows walk-ins no more than five documents or sets at a time. The tax office stamps the deed before the clerk records it, so leave a couple of days between the two.

sections.h2: Sellers who live out of state
sections.html:
If you live outside Maryland, 8.75% of the total payment is held back at settlement when you are an individual, and 8.25% when you are an entity. Form MW506NRS reports the withholding, and recording waits for the payment.

Think of it as an advance on your income tax rather than a true closing cost. An early refund request is available if you owe less and the price is under $1.5 million. Our Maryland capital gains guide has the full rules.

sections.h2: Closing costs in a direct cash sale
sections.html:
Paying cash does not shrink these charges, since they attach to the deed and the tax account. What a cash contract decides is who covers each line.

Ask for a written net sheet with every tax line itemized before you sign. Then confirm three things with your attorney or title company: first-time buyer status, which party pays the county transfer and recordation taxes, and the balance the county shows on the tax account.

On closing day the order of events is predictable. The title company or attorney collects the tax certificate, the deed goes to the county tax office for a stamp, and then it moves to the clerk for recording. The taxes and fees come out of your proceeds unless the contract assigns them to the buyer, so the net sheet is the only way to know what you will actually receive. Keep a copy of the recorded deed and the final settlement statement for your own tax records.

faqs.a: Absent a contrary contract term, each party pays half of the State and local transfer taxes and the recordation tax. With a first-time buyer moving in, the seller covers the full State tax and, by default, the local taxes.

faqs.q: What is the State transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: Half a percent (0.5%) of consideration. A first-time Maryland buyer who will occupy the home pays the lower 0.25% rate, all of it paid by the seller.

faqs.q: How much is the recordation tax in Maryland?
faqs.a: It depends on the county, per $500 of consideration: $2.50 in Howard and Baltimore Counties, $3.30 in Harford and $7.00 in Frederick.

faqs.q: Do Maryland sellers pay a recording fee?
faqs.a: Yes, a $20 fee for most short deeds plus a $40 surcharge. The contract says who bears it.

faqs.q: Does property tax have to be paid before closing?
faqs.a: Yes. Everything owed must be paid and the collector's certificate endorsed on the deed before the county posts the transfer.
